issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts hard or fails
issues.sym: Harsh or banging shifts, flaring revs between gears, a "transmission service required" message, slipping, or limp mode stuck in one gear.
issues.why: The 5-speed AW55-50 automatic used in these years wears its valve body and pressure solenoids, and Volvo issued several bulletins for harsh shifts. Transmission failure is the top complaint for 2001-2004 V70 and XC70 wagons.
issues.next: Get the codes read and ask about software updates and an adaptation reset. If it slips or won't engage, stop hard driving and get a transmission diagnosis.

issues.t: AWD angle gear wears out and leaks
issues.sym: A whine or grinding from the front, a gear oil smell or leak near the passenger side of the engine, or loss of drive with a whirring sound.
issues.why: The angle gear that sends power to the rear wheels sits next to the hot exhaust; its oil breaks down and the gears and seals wear.
issues.next: Check for leaks and change the angle gear oil. A noisy or failed unit needs a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: AWD stops sending power to the rear wheels
issues.sym: The wagon drives like front-wheel drive, spins its front tires in snow, or shows an AWD warning.
issues.why: The Haldex coupling's electric pump or controller fails, often because its fluid and filter were never changed.
issues.next: Have the AWD system scanned and the Haldex pump tested. Service the fluid regularly afterward.

issues.t: AWD system disabled warning (Haldex pump or coupling)
issues.sym: An "AWD service required" or "AWD disabled" message, and the car drives on the front wheels only.
issues.why: The electric pump in the Haldex coupling wears or clogs, especially when the fluid and filter are never changed.
issues.next: Have the AWD codes read. A new pump, filter and fluid often fixes it; change the Haldex fluid about every 30,000-40,000 miles.

issues.t: Clogged PCV system pushes out oil seals
issues.sym: Oil leaks from cam seals, rear main seal or oil pan, a whistle or moan at idle, or high oil use.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) oil trap and hoses clog with sludge, building pressure inside the engine that pushes oil past seals.
issues.next: Fix the PCV system before replacing leaking seals, or the new seals will leak too.

issues.t: ABS module fails and turns on warning lights
issues.sym: ABS and traction warning lights, "Anti-skid service required", and sometimes a dead speedometer or cruise control.
issues.why: Solder joints inside the ABS control module crack with heat and age.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A rebuilt or resoldered module costs much less than new.

issues.t: Central electronic module (CEM) faults
issues.sym: Random electrical problems, lots of warning messages at once, or a car that cranks but won't start.
issues.why: The central electronic module's circuit board and relays can fail, often after water gets in.
issues.next: Have a Volvo specialist scan all modules. A repaired or replacement CEM must be programmed to the car.

issues.t: Worn front control arm bushings
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, shimmy when braking, and loose-feeling steering.
issues.why: Control arm bushings, strut mounts and ball joints are the most-reported repairs on these wagons.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected; new control arms and an alignment are the usual fix.

issues.t: Turbo leaks oil onto the exhaust
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning oil smell from under the hood, and oil on the turbo or exhaust.
issues.why: Turbo oil feed and return lines and seals leak with age.
issues.next: Have the leak found and fixed quickly; oil on a hot exhaust can catch fire.

issues.t: Oil leaks from vacuum pump and valve cover
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell, or oil on the side of the engine.
issues.why: On the six-cylinder engines the brake vacuum pump seals can blow out and the valve cover sealant weakens with age.
issues.next: Have the leak found before oil reaches hot exhaust parts. A vacuum pump seal kit is far cheaper than a new pump.

issues.t: Hissing at idle from torn PCV diaphragm
issues.sym: Hissing at idle, rough idle, a lean check engine code, or oil seal leaks.
issues.why: The rubber diaphragm in the 3.0L turbo's PCV valve tears with age.
issues.next: Replace the PCV unit if you hear hissing at idle.

issues.t: Low oil level warning from faulty dipstick
issues.sym: Oil seems to disappear and an "Engine Oil Level Low" message comes on.
issues.why: Volvo bulletin TJ30021 found the dipstick could let oil escape; it replaces the dipstick and updates engine software.
issues.next: Top up the oil and ask a dealer whether TJ30021 was done.

issues.t: Engine burns oil from faulty piston rings
issues.sym: Adding oil between changes, low oil warnings, smoke at startup, and in bad cases power loss or engine failure.
issues.why: The oil control rings can fail to clear oil from the cylinder walls, so it burns. A class action covers 2013-2016 Volvos with these 2.0L and 2.5L engines, naming the XC70.
issues.next: Check the oil often and ask a dealer for an oil consumption test; failing engines need new pistons and rings.

issues.t: Door won't lock or unlock with the remote
issues.sym: A door doesn't respond to the key fob or buzzes when locking.
issues.why: The electric actuator in the door lock wears out; rear doors are common on these wagons.
issues.next: Have the latch tested and replaced.

issues.t: Sunroof drains clog and leak water inside
issues.sym: Wet front carpets, water dripping from the headliner, or a musty smell.
issues.why: The sunroof drain tubes clog, so rain overflows into the cabin.
issues.next: Clear the drains and dry the carpet quickly to protect wiring and modules.

issues.t: Throttle body fault causes stalling and limp mode (recall)
issues.sym: Rough idle, loss of power, stalling in traffic, and a warning light as the car drops into limp-home mode.
issues.why: The electronic throttle module wore internally. Regulators pressed Volvo to extend its warranty, and recall 06V-441 updated software to stop needless limp mode.
issues.next: Check for recall 06V-441. A throttle body that still fails needs replacement.

issues.t: Headlight switch can cut out headlights (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights flicker or go out.
issues.why: A faulty headlight switch.
issues.next: Have recalls 99V-235 and 04V-504 checked.

issues.t: Turn signals may not flash (recall)
issues.sym: Turn signals don't blink when used.
issues.why: A defect in the turn signal circuit.
issues.next: Have recall 00V-405 done.

issues.t: Passenger airbag could deploy by itself (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag light may come on; the passenger airbag could go off without a crash.
issues.why: A defect in the passenger airbag system.
issues.next: Have recall 99V-236 done.

issues.t: Electric cooling fan can overheat and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: The fan motor and controller could overheat.
issues.next: Have recall 04V-451 done.

issues.t: Tailgate may not lock properly (recall)
issues.sym: The tailgate doesn't stay latched or locked.
issues.why: A defect in the tailgate locking mechanism.
issues.next: Have recall 00V-239 done.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash the driver airbag can burst and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: The inflator's propellant breaks down over years of heat and humidity.
issues.next: Stop driving and contact a Volvo dealer if recall 21V-800 is open on your VIN.

issues.t: Fuel pump flange can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell, especially in hot weather.
issues.why: The plastic flange on top of the fuel pump can crack.
issues.next: Have recall 09V-483 checked; a fuel leak is a fire risk.

issues.t: Fuel pressure sensor can cause misfires and stalling (recall)
issues.sym: Misfires, loss of power, or stalling.
issues.why: Solder joints in the fuel pressure sensor can crack.
issues.next: Have recall 07V-226 done.

issues.t: Front seat belt anchor cable can break (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; the belt may not hold in a crash.
issues.why: The steel cable anchoring the front belts can fatigue and snap.
issues.next: Have recall 20V-378 done.

issues.t: Cooling fan may stop and engine can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Temperature gauge climbing, overheating warnings.
issues.why: A software error in the fan control module could stop the radiator fan.
issues.next: Have recall 09V-218 done.

issues.t: Fuel pump module may not get signal and engine stalls (recall)
issues.sym: Hard starting or stalling.
issues.why: Central electronic module software could fail to signal the fuel pump module.
issues.next: Have recall 09V-343 done.

issues.t: Driver airbag clockspring connector fault (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light; the driver airbag might not deploy.
issues.why: An intermittent fault in the steering wheel clockspring connector.
issues.next: Have recall 10V-489 done.

issues.t: Engine can stall suddenly from software fuel cut-off (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off without warning.
issues.why: The engine computer cut fuel too readily.
issues.next: Have recall 10V-579 done.

issues.t: Seat wiring can disconnect and affect airbags (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light after moving a seat.
issues.why: The seat wiring harness could come apart during seat adjustment.
issues.next: Have recall 12V-075 done.

issues.t: False tire pressure service message (recall)
issues.sym: "TPMS Service Required" appears and the car won't warn of low tires.
issues.why: A software error in the tire pressure monitoring system.
issues.next: Check tire pressures by hand and have recall 12V-415 done.

issues.t: Wipers run nonstop and lights can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers keep running; turn signals and high beams stop working.
issues.why: A fault in the central electronic module.
issues.next: Have recall 13V-377 done.

issues.t: Starter fuse can blow with stop/start (recall)
issues.sym: After an auto stop, the engine may not restart.
issues.why: The starter fuse could blow from repeated stop/start use.
issues.next: Have recall 15V-555 done.
